terms.definition: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water; releases energy and takes place mainly in the mitochondria.
terms.examiner: Respiration is exothermic and happens all the time in living cells.

terms.definition: glucose → lactic acid, when there is not enough oxygen; releases much less energy than aerobic respiration.
terms.examiner: The glucose is only partly oxidised.

terms.definition: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide; called fermentation.
terms.examiner: Used to make bread and alcoholic drinks.

terms.definition: The amount of extra oxygen the body needs after exercise to react with the lactic acid and remove it from cells.
terms.examiner: Higher tier: lactic acid is taken to the liver and converted back to glucose.

terms.definition: Muscles stop contracting efficiently during long periods of vigorous activity.
terms.examiner: Lactic acid build-up and lack of oxygen are the causes.

terms.definition: The sum of all the reactions in a cell or the body.
terms.examiner: Includes making starch, cellulose, lipids and proteins, respiration, and breaking down excess proteins into urea.
